# rind on `amd-ryzen-9-5900xt`: AMD Ryzen 9 5900XT 16-Core Processor

- OS: Oracle Linux Server 10.3 (Linux 6.12.0-208.112.5.3.el10uek.x86_64)

## Gaps

Each operation where another library is more than 10% faster than rind, by rind's rule (OpenSSL counts), with its reason from [gaps.toml](gaps.toml). `cargo xtask host-report` refuses a gap without an entry and an entry that covers no gap.

| Operations | rind over the fastest | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `mlkem768-keygen` | 1.25× verified-garbage | 1.25x pyca/verified-garbage on the medians of three runs. Upstream decided this in kixel-ai/rind#812 (benchmarks/gaps.toml, on nixos, the same Ryzen 9 5900XT): on x86_64 without AVX-512 ML-KEM-768 key generation stays on rind's arithmetic because decapsulation, the hot path, runs on the arithmetic that generated the key and VG's decapsulation was 1.17-1.25x slower. |
| `p384-ecdsa-sign` | 1.11× verified-garbage | 1.11x pyca/verified-garbage on the medians of three runs, on a host sharing its CPU with a vLLM job (busy_share relaxed to 0.15; see relaxations.json). Upstream records the same 1.06-1.11x margin on ovh-iad, ovh-sea and fedora: rind's hedged per-signature nonce (fresh randomness, as aws-lc-rs) against VG's deterministic RFC 6979 nonce is deliberate, so it stays. |
| `sha1/64B` | 1.18× RustCrypto + dalek | 1.18x RustCrypto at 64 B only on the medians of three runs. Upstream keeps SHA-1 as a legacy-only algorithm without a speed quest (benchmarks/gaps.toml, sha1/* on portable); a 64 B hash is fixed-cost dominated and this host was shared with a vLLM job. |
